title: Introduction
description: A familiar way to explore. A different kind of ownership.

sections.title: Meet OpenXplorer
paragraphs: OpenXplorer is a Windows File Explorer-inspired file manager for Linux, built for Zorin OS and intended to extend to compatible Ubuntu and Debian installations. It brings a familiar tabbed interface to your local folders and SMB shares.
Previously called Winspace, the project is now published as OpenXplorer. The desktop application and this website are distributed under AGPL-3.0-only; original third-party notices remain intact.
sections.imageAlt: OpenXplorer showing the sample Documents folder, with Launch planning selected and pinned to Quick access

sections.title: Your files. Your network. Your workflow.
paragraphs: Navigate with clickable breadcrumbs, pin folders, type to select a filename, resize columns, and use either a classic or compact context menu. Search opted-in filename indexes, browse ZIP contents read-only, and inspect existing exposed snapshots.

The tour below shows pictures of the real native app, captured with fictional sample files: click a control in a picture to see where it leads. It cannot access your computer, NAS, browser settings or keyring. On a desktop-sized screen, use the buttons above the tour to open a scene, switch appearance, or play a short walkthrough. The tour is not loaded on phones; the documentation and screenshots remain available.
items: Local files and SMB shares in one interface.
A searchable Settings page, with explicit controls for desktop integration.
Source included alongside the installer; no account needed to use the app.

sections.title: Native storage. Local interface.
paragraphs: Since 2.0.0 the desktop app is a native GTK 4 application written in Rust. GIO/GVfs provides the filesystem, SMB and phone layer; SQLite stores the optional filename index. The Python/WebKitGTK app of 1.x is retired; its last release, 1.1.4, stays available as a tag of the public repository. This Next.js website is separate and is not required to run the app; its tour shows pictures of the native app.

sections.title: Know what you are installing
paragraphs: Version 2.0.0 replaces the Python app with the native GTK 4 app under the same name, settings and saved passwords, and adds Fluent icons, a categorised Settings page, undo, and Flatpak and distribution packages. Zorin is the primary target; Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 13, Fedora, openSUSE and Arch are supported through their packages, and every other distribution through the Flatpak. Version 2.0.1 adds split panes, a Compact view, a folder tree, thumbnails, transfer jobs with undo, SFTP, FTP, WebDAV and NFS locations, content search and optional Open and Save dialogs for other apps. Version 2.0.2 opens ZIPs like folders, makes Extract all and the Open and Save dialogs work as in Windows, and adds Windows 11's Compact view and collapsible This PC and Network sections. Version 2.0.3 adds Windows Explorer's Group by, separate from the sort, makes copies ask about a single unreadable file and about names Windows cannot use, and says when a drive is read-only or a tab's drive or share goes away. Version 2.0.4 adds item check boxes as in Windows 11 and a redesigned Settings page, with a search across every page. Version 2.0.5 names copies, drags files and makes new folders as Windows Explorer does, shows Size on disk in Properties, asks before a rename changes an extension, lets Super+E open it on KDE Plasma, and shows an empty folder as Windows does, taking right-click, paste and drops there. Version 2.0.6 lets Brave's downloads, Save as PDF and uploads open OpenXplorer's Open and Save dialogs, and can make Brave ask where to save each download, by default shows an unselected item's check box on hover only while Ctrl is held, as Windows Explorer does, and can index frequently opened folders for instant search (experimental, off by default). Version 2.0.7 sends other apps' Open and Save dialogs, GTK 3 apps' included, to OpenXplorer as part of Make OpenXplorer default, formats removable drives in its own Format dialog, and deletes files on shares faster. Version 2.0.8 adds Windows Explorer's Folder Options, its Ctrl+E, Ctrl+D, F11 and Alt+P keys, and a Share button that emails the selected files, moves deleted items to the Recycle Bin wherever that works, and, as Windows Explorer does, no longer shows a message, an Undo button or a desktop notification after a file operation that succeeds or is cancelled, while failures are still reported. The known gaps are listed in the changelog. Version 2.0.9 keeps a name being renamed in place open through its own right-click menu, and item check boxes are off by default, so a selected item is only highlighted, and a search word found only in a name's extension no longer matches. Version 2.0.10 adds a Simplified Chinese translation, used when the desktop's language is Chinese; every other language stays in English. Version 2.0.11 keeps a shown search's results still while the search cache changes, so a selected result stays selected. Version 2.0.12 shows running copies, moves and deletes in a Windows-style progress window, redoes Properties as Windows 11's Properties windows, renames several selected items at once, creates a text document and renames it in place, drags tabs as Chrome does, makes search faster, and refuses an administrator delete of a folder that other accounts can change. Version 2.0.13 also refuses an administrator folder delete on a drive an ordinary user can mount or plug in. Version 2.0.14 deletes those folders as administrator again, through a helper that holds each folder open while it empties it, says when a new release is out, and no longer crashes when a tab is dragged out on Wayland.
sections.callout: Use a disposable folder and a non-critical share first. SMB servers other than the maintainer's, phones and USB drives have not yet been accepted on real hardware with the native app.

sections.title: Start with one folder
paragraphs: Read Installation, open your home directory, and test a network share. Enable indexing and default-file-manager integration only after checking basic file operations.

title: Installation
description: Install the stable release without replacing your desktop.

sections.title: Requirements
paragraphs: For the .deb: Zorin OS 18, Ubuntu 24.04 or newer, or Debian 13 on x86-64, with GTK 4.14 or newer, GIO/GVfs and a graphical user session. The .deb declares its runtime dependencies; APT resolves them. Fedora, openSUSE and Arch users install the release's .rpm or Arch package when it lists one; every other distribution, including Debian 12, uses the Flatpak bundle.

There are no Node.js, pnpm or Python requirements for the application itself. The optional persistent mount helper, openxplorer-mount-share, is a Rust program in the .deb, .rpm and Arch packages (not the Flatpak); it needs cifs-utils.

sections.title: Install OpenXplorer
paragraphs: Close every old Winspace/OpenXplorer window and finish file operations. Download the .deb, then run these commands from that download directory as your normal user.
sections.code:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install ./openxplorer_2.0.14_all.deb
openxplorer --version
openxplorer
sections.callout: This is a local unsigned package, not an APT repository. Installation does not change your default file manager, Downloads folder, browser preferences, or network mounts.

sections.title: Update from inside the app
paragraphs: Once a day, a few seconds after OpenXplorer starts, it asks the public OpenXplorer GitHub Releases API whether a newer release exists. When one does, a notice pops up at the top right with Install update… and Later, an accent Update button shows in the command bar beside the Settings gear, and Update available shows at the bottom right, beside the view controls. Later only closes that release's notice; Update and Update available stay until you update. You can also check at any time with Settings › About › Check for updates, and turn the daily check off there with Check for updates automatically. In 2.0.13 and earlier the app checked only when you asked, and in 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 the button is at the bottom of the sidebar. Review the installed and available versions, then choose Install update. Finish file operations and tab moves first.

The installed Debian app downloads the release installer, verifies its GitHub SHA-256 digest and package identity, then asks for system administrator approval through polkit. APT installs the update without removing packages. Choose Restart now when finished; restarting closes existing windows and tabs.

Older releases need one manual upgrade to 1.1.0 before this control is available; 1.1.x offers the newest 2.x release there. Earlier releases need one manual upgrade from GitHub Releases. Source checkouts, RPM, Arch and Flatpak installations update through their own package manager. Updates are not live code patches; the running app must restart. GitHub HTTPS and asset digests are the trust boundary, not an independent publisher signature. To go back to 1.1.4, install its .deb with sudo apt install --allow-downgrades; settings and saved passwords are shared.

sections.title: Upgrading from Winspace
paragraphs: The new package replaces winspace-explorer versions older than 0.8.0. Existing settings, caches, desktop IDs and credential identifiers are deliberately retained. The winspace and winspace-mount-share commands are compatibility aliases.

Stop the previous background reveal service before upgrading: winspace --quit. Do not force-kill a process that is transferring files. Re-pin the installed OpenXplorer launcher if the dock has cached the old display name.

sections.title: First-run checklist
paragraphs: Open a disposable folder. Create and rename a test file, then send it to Trash. Connect to a non-critical SMB share before trusting the app with your main storage. For a phone, unlock it and select file transfer or trust the computer when prompted; a GVfs-supported device then appears under This PC. See Known limitations in the project README before enabling advanced operations.

sections.title: Blank window or graphics trouble
paragraphs: Close the application completely and try the software-rendering launch. This changes this launch only, not your desktop graphics configuration.

sections.title: Remove the application
paragraphs: In Settings, restore previous default handlers, disable Show in folder integration and, on KDE Plasma, turn off Super+E opens OpenXplorer before removal, so Super+E goes back to the app that had it. Unmount/remove persistent mounts separately after closing files. Removing the application does not undo custom folder locations or delete your files.

sections.title: The Software card before installation
paragraphs: A downloaded .deb can have a generic card before installation even though its installed card shows the folder icon, application name and AGPL license. The embedded catalog is not necessarily available to Software until installed and indexed. Another icon or homepage URL cannot guarantee the local pre-install view.

A signed repository with a pre-indexed AppStream catalog can supply that information before installation. This project does not configure or deploy such a repository as part of installing the local package.

title: SMB & network shares
description: Browse your network without losing your sense of place.

sections.title: Connect to a server
paragraphs: Type a server or share address in the address bar, or open Network to see the computers on your network and open one. The address bar also accepts Linux paths, UNC paths and smb:// locations. Each breadcrumb is separately clickable.

Windows-style paths use backslashes, not backticks: \\studio-nas\Projects. You can also use smb://studio-nas/Projects. Click each breadcrumb to jump to an ancestor. The website walkthrough uses this exact interface; the website itself makes no SMB connections.

A slow server shows that it is working, as Windows Explorer does: the address bar fills with progress and Refresh turns into Stop at once, and after a moment the file list says Working on it... in place of the previous folder. Press Stop, or Esc while you are still in the address bar, to cancel and stay where you were. Pressing Enter again does not start over; entering another address replaces the slow one. Other tabs stay usable meanwhile.
sections.imageAlt: The Network page with its address box, and the sample share \\studio-nas\Projects saved (shown offline in this picture)

sections.title: Sign in, once per server when possible
paragraphs: The in-app prompt, Enter network credentials, asks for a user name and password, as Windows does. Remember my credentials requests persistent system-keyring storage. When unchecked, reusable credentials are scoped to the Linux login session if the Secret Service session collection is available.

Accounts are scoped by server and port. Different host aliases, rejected credentials, or shares requiring another account may prompt again. A locked keyring can show an operating-system unlock dialog; it is not the SMB credential prompt.

sections.title: Keep a share in reach
paragraphs: Map network drive, below the navigation pane or in the … menu of This PC and Network, asks for a drive letter and a folder such as \\studio-nas\Projects, as in Windows 11. Reconnect at sign-in saves the share beneath Network; on Linux the letter is only part of its name, such as Projects (Z:). Connect using different credentials asks for an account even when one is saved. Its link Connect to a Web site opens Add a network location, which also connects SFTP, FTP, WebDAV and NFS folders.

Successfully browsed locations appear beneath Network for the session. Right-click a share and choose Keep in Network to save it. Pin a share or a nested folder into the sidebar for a direct route back. Green marks indicate network-backed locations, not guaranteed online status.

The picture shows the sidebar with the sample folder Launch planning pinned to Quick access and the saved share Projects under Network. It was captured from the native app with fictional files and no network, so the share is shown offline.
sections.imageAlt: The sidebar with the sample Launch planning folder pinned to Quick access and the saved share Projects under Network

sections.title: Discover nearby servers
paragraphs: Network lists the computers and servers that advertise themselves on your network, as Windows 11 does, through the installed GVfs discovery providers. It looks each time you open it, and Refresh looks again. Devices must advertise themselves and be reachable through your network and firewall. It does not scan every IP address or guarantee an exhaustive list. If Network says that network discovery is turned off, the GVfs network services are missing; type the server's address instead.

sections.title: Bookmarks are not persistent mounts
paragraphs: For a Downloads location or an application that needs a filesystem path, use a persistent CIFS mount. A bookmark such as smb://nas/Downloads is a browsing shortcut, not a system-wide mount. The optional mount helper requires reviewed, explicit administrative action.

sections.title: Sign out safely
paragraphs: Finish operations and close files on the server first. Sign out can disconnect matching desktop-session SMB mounts used by other applications. Forgetting saved credentials and removing filename-cache entries are separate choices; neither deletes server files.

title: Search & indexing
description: Search names and paths from a local index. Keep the boundaries clear.

sections.title: Choose what gets indexed
paragraphs: Settings → Search → Indexed folders → Manage lists folders, SMB shares and mounted volumes. Check a root or add a custom path to index its filenames and metadata. The initial scan does not download file contents. Settings → Search → Cache this folder for search indexes the folder you opened Settings from, as a folder's right-click menu does.
Each mounted filesystem is selected separately. Selecting Local Disk does not automatically traverse every other mounted volume.

sections.title: Local events, network checks
paragraphs: Local selected directories use filesystem watches while the app is open. Network shares use incremental directory checks, not SMB server-side push notifications. After the app has been closed, reconciliation catches missed changes.

sections.title: Results open their real locations
paragraphs: A result includes its parent path. Opening a directory navigates to the actual folder; opening a file checks current metadata and launches an appropriate application. As in Windows 11, a search is a step of the tab’s history: the tab and address bar read Search Results in Documents, Back returns to the folder, Forward to the results, and Back from a folder opened from them shows them again. Emptying the search box also goes back to the folder. Stale results can remain when a server is offline.
sections.imageAlt: A cached search for “budget” in the native app, showing the folder of the result

sections.title: Coverage and limits
paragraphs: The current implementation limits an initial root scan to one million entries, watches up to 8,192 local directories, and uses timed fallback beyond watch coverage. Search displays the first 500 matches and indicates truncation. System/temporary trees, snapshot collections, links and nested mounts are excluded from whole-disk traversal.

sections.title: The index stays on your machine
paragraphs: The database contains filenames and paths, which can be sensitive. Disable a root to remove its indexed records. An overlapping root can still contain the same names. The cache is not encrypted and is not an offline copy of file contents.

sections.title: Need a nearby file? Just type.
paragraphs: Click the current file list and type SC to select a loaded filename beginning with those letters. This does not filter the view, search subfolders, or contact the NAS for each keystroke. Press Enter to open it.

title: Default file manager
description: Make explicit changes, with a way back.

sections.title: Set folder and SMB handlers
paragraphs: Settings → Default apps → Make OpenXplorer default changes the per-user folder and SMB associations and records previous handlers. With Also handle Open and Save dialogs, which starts on, it also sends other apps’ file pickers, such as Brave’s uploads and Save dialogs, to OpenXplorer (see Open and Save dialogs below); click Apply now beside Open and Save dialogs, or log out and back in, for them to follow. If the card says OpenXplorer is your default file explorer, except for Open and Save dialogs, click Make OpenXplorer default again with that option on. Installing the package does not do this for you.

sections.title: Brave: Show in folder
paragraphs: Opening the ZIP filename in Brave and Show in folder are different actions. ZIP opening uses an archive association; Show in folder may use a desktop portal, FileManager1, or the default directory handler. Folder defaults alone do not prove either browser route is configured.

Settings shows separate statuses for folders, SMB links, ZIP files and the current FileManager1 owner. Keep Include Brave / other apps’ Show in folder integration checked when applying folder defaults. If ownership says waiting for another file manager, finish operations and close that app; log out and back in if necessary. OpenXplorer does not kill it.

Restart Brave after changing handlers. Test Show in folder checks FileManager1, not Brave’s portal. A browser portal can retain a different choice; select OpenXplorer in its chooser when available. Do not disable the system portal. To pick and save files in OpenXplorer too, see Open and Save dialogs below.

sections.title: Open ZIP downloads in OpenXplorer
paragraphs: In Settings → ZIP & archives, click Use OpenXplorer for ZIPs. This is an explicit, per-user change to ZIP associations; Settings → Default apps → Undo and troubleshooting has the Restore ZIP handler button. It does not change PDF, video, or document defaults. Installation never changes these associations.
A ZIP opens in the built-in ZIP browser; this setting does not automatically extract it. You can instead leave ZIPs assigned to an external archive manager.
sections.code:
xdg-mime query default inode/directory
xdg-mime query default application/zip
openxplorer --diagnose

sections.title: Open and Save dialogs
paragraphs: Settings → Default apps → Other apps' Open and Save dialogs → Enable, or Make OpenXplorer default with Also handle Open and Save dialogs on, makes other applications choose and save files in an OpenXplorer window: the same navigation pane, address bar and search, with File name, Save as type and the Save or Open button at the bottom. It works for applications that use the desktop portal for file dialogs, such as Chrome, Brave, GTK 4 apps and Flatpak apps, and, from your next login, GTK 3 apps (see below); applications that draw their own dialog keep it. As in Windows, the File name box takes a name, a path from the folder shown, ~/… or a full path: a folder opens, a file is chosen, and Save adds the chosen type’s extension unless the name has it already or ends in another known type’s (so “Notes v2.1” is saved as “Notes v2.1.pdf”); choosing another Save as type changes the name’s extension to the new type’s. A file typed in the address bar is chosen too. Escape and Ctrl+Q cancel the dialog, Alt+Left, Alt+Right and Alt+Up work from the File name box, and Ctrl+N opens no other window.

Enabling writes one preference into your own desktop-portal configuration (the file the portal reads now, or a new ~/.config/xdg-desktop-portal/<desktop>-portals.conf) and records what the file held; every other portal, such as screenshots or screen sharing, keeps its backend. If the portal service is set to read one folder only (XDG_DESKTOP_PORTAL_DIR in its environment, which some tools set to add a portal of their own), OpenXplorer works in that folder instead: it adds its line to the file the portal reads there, or a new file holding only that line, and links its packaged .portal file there, and Restore removes both again. Click Apply now to restart the desktop portal when it runs as a user service, or log out and back in. Saving over an existing file always asks first.

GTK 3 apps show GTK’s own dialog unless told to use the portal, so Enable also adds ~/.config/environment.d/60-openxplorer-file-dialogs.conf, which sets GTK_USE_PORTAL=1 for your session when you log in. Only a desktop session the systemd user manager starts (GNOME, and KDE Plasma by default) reads that file, so OpenXplorer adds it only there, while graphical-session.target is active; on other desktops, such as Xfce or MATE, GTK 3 apps keep GTK’s dialog. GTK 3 apps follow after you log out and back in; Restore removes the file again. If you enabled the dialogs with an earlier version, the status line says Click Enable for GTK 3 apps too; Enable, or Make OpenXplorer default, adds the file. If a file of yours already has that name, OpenXplorer leaves it alone and the status line says GTK 3 apps keep GTK’s dialog.

On KDE Plasma, KDE’s own apps (Plasma and its widgets, Kate, System Settings and the rest) show their own dialog unless told to use the portal, so Enable also adds ~/.config/plasma-workspace/env/openxplorer-file-dialogs.sh, which sets PLASMA_INTEGRATION_USE_PORTAL=1 when you log in. KDE apps follow after you log out and back in; Restore removes the file again. If a file of yours already has that name, OpenXplorer leaves it alone and the status line says KDE apps keep KDE’s dialog.

Restore Open and Save dialogs puts the file back as it was, or, if you edited it since, removes only OpenXplorer’s line. The Flatpak cannot change the host’s portal, so this is available in the installed package only.

Each application’s dialogs remember the folder you last chose a file in, one folder per application, shared by its Open and Save dialogs, as Windows does, and still there after a restart. As in Windows, a dialog opens in that folder while the application suggests the same folder as the first time (or none); a different folder the application suggests is honoured, a file it names with its full path opens that file’s folder, and with nothing to go on the dialog opens Documents. A remembered folder that no longer exists, or a network share that is not connected or stopped answering, is passed over within a second or two without an error. An application is told apart by the ID the desktop portal gives it, or else by its program’s file name (such as chrome); one that cannot be named is not remembered. The folders are kept in ~/.config/winspace/dialog-folders.json, readable by you only, and a network folder is kept as its address without any user name or password, for example smb://nas.example/projects/Reports.

Saving to a network folder works through the share’s local path that GVfs provides (its FUSE folder under /run/user/<id>/gvfs), which applications such as Chrome need: the dialog answers with that file:// path. Before the dialog answers a Save, it checks that the folder takes new files by creating a file of its own there, with an ordinary name, and removing it again, much as Windows does, so a read-only share says “You don’t have permission to save in this location.” and a share that disconnected says it is not available, instead of the save seeming to succeed. Without GVfs’s FUSE folder (the gvfs-fuse package on Debian and Ubuntu), the dialog says to choose a folder on this computer or a connected drive.

sections.title: Super+E on KDE Plasma
paragraphs: On KDE Plasma, turn on Settings → Default apps → Keyboard shortcut → Super+E opens OpenXplorer to make Super+E open a new OpenXplorer window, as Win+E opens a new File Explorer window in Windows, whether or not one is already open. Plasma gives Super+E to Dolphin; OpenXplorer asks KDE's shortcut service to move it, keeps Dolphin's other shortcuts, and records which app had it in its settings folder. The change shows in System Settings → Shortcuts and lasts across logins.

Log out and back in after turning it on or off: Plasma follows the new Super+E only from the next login. Turning it off gives Super+E back to the app that had it; if you have given Super+E to another app since, it is left alone. Other desktops and the Flatpak do not offer this.

sections.title: What this does not replace
paragraphs: Browsers can route reveal actions through desktop portals or keep a previous application choice. Choose OpenXplorer in a chooser when available. Upload/save file-picker dialogs stay with the system unless you turn on Open and Save dialogs, alone or with Make OpenXplorer default. On other desktops Super+E stays a separate desktop keyboard shortcut; the app changes it only on KDE Plasma, when you turn on Super+E (above).

sections.title: Tabs, windows and the taskbar
paragraphs: Drag a tab onto another OpenXplorer window’s tab strip to merge it, or drop it outside to create a window. You can also right-click the tab and choose Move tab to window… to select an existing destination. The original is kept until the destination accepts the tab. Close this tab’s dialog and finish file operations first.

The installed launcher offers New window, Open windows and Settings. File dragging uses its own native GTK transport: drop selected files into compatible applications, or into an OpenXplorer folder to confirm a copy. Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X/Ctrl+V remain available, including GNOME and KDE file clipboards. Native Wayland and individual application behavior need confirmation on the target desktop.

sections.title: Restore the previous setup
paragraphs: Disable Show in folder removes only OpenXplorer’s unmodified user-level service files. Restore previous also restores recorded file associations and gives Open and Save dialogs back to the desktop. Modified or third-party configuration is preserved for manual review. Restore Open and Save dialogs gives file dialogs back to the desktop the same way.

title: Downloads & Brave
description: A familiar Location tab, with Linux filesystem semantics.

sections.title: Set a standard folder location
paragraphs: Right-click Downloads or Documents → Properties → Location. Choose an existing writable directory, check the destination, and confirm before applying. The previous user-directory setting is backed up. No existing files are moved, merged or deleted.

sections.title: Use a stable mount for a network destination
paragraphs: Use a persistent Linux mount path such as /mnt/nas/downloads. Temporary per-login GVfs paths and an unmounted SMB URL are not suitable replacements for a standard folder.
sections.callout: An offline NAS cannot accept a download. The search index is not an offline synchronization engine.

sections.title: Optionally sync native Brave profiles
paragraphs: Also update Brave’s download directory opens a separate profile-selection and confirmation step. Fully quit Brave, including background processes, first. Only download and Save As directory fields are changed, with private backups and field-level restoration. Optionally, Ask where to save each file before downloading also turns on Brave’s own setting of that name, so each download opens a Save dialog first: OpenXplorer’s when Other apps’ Open and Save dialogs is enabled in Settings → Default apps. Restore previous puts that setting back too, unless you changed it since.

sections.title: Sandboxed or custom browser profiles
paragraphs: For unsupported Flatpak/Snap, custom or policy-managed profiles, set the same mounted path manually in Brave. Filesystem access permissions may also need review.

sections.title: Review the optional mount helper
paragraphs: The optional helper prepares persistent systemd mount/automount configuration. It needs administrator approval and uses a root-readable plaintext CIFS credential file, separate from the desktop keyring. It is not invoked during package installation. The stable packages install it as /usr/bin/openxplorer-mount-share (the Flatpak cannot), and the mount assistant in a folder's Location tab prints the command for an administrator to run; the app never runs it. Read "Mount helper" in native/packaging/README.md before using it.

title: Interface & snapshots
description: Make the workspace fit the way you work.

sections.title: Your workspace, your widths
paragraphs: Resize the sidebar and column edges. Double-click an edge to reset or fit it, depending on the control. Width preferences survive restarts. Local and SMB ancestors remain individual breadcrumb buttons. As in Windows 11, the arrow before the first one lists Home, This PC, Network and the Recycle Bin, the arrow after each one lists all of its subfolders, and on a long path the first ones fold into a « button that lists them.
sections.imageAlt: Historical directory in an amber-badged Previous version tab, with a read-only banner

sections.title: Choose a folder view
paragraphs: View offers Details, List, icon sizes, Tiles and Content. Use Ctrl+mouse wheel or the icon sizes in View to change icon size; as in Windows, the wheel steps through Details, List and the icon sizes but not Tiles or Content. Tiles shows each item's icon with its name, type and size beside it, in columns that fill the window; Content lists one item per row, its name and type beside its icon and its date modified and size at the right. Settings → Files & folders → Expandable folders in Details lets Details expand folders in place (off by default, as in Windows Explorer); drag from empty space to select items, hold Ctrl to toggle them or Shift to add them. In Details, as in Windows, the part of a row past the end of its name (and its Date, Type and Size columns) counts as empty space while the row is not selected: drag from there to select rows even when the folder fills the window, or click there to clear the selection. View → Compact view, also in Settings → Appearance → Files and folders, draws the Details rows and the navigation pane closer together, as in Windows 11, so more items fit. View → Item check boxes, on by default as in Windows 11, gives each item a check box that shows while you point at it and stays checked while it is selected; click it to select or deselect that item alone, or use the box before Name in Details to select every item, and again to select none.

Right-click a Details heading to choose columns, then drag headings to reorder them. The Recycle Bin includes Original location and Date deleted. Sort is laid out like Windows Explorer’s: Name, Date modified and Type, with Size and the other file properties under More. Sort › Group by groups the folder apart from its sort, so a folder grouped by date modified can be sorted by name within each group: choose Name (A – H, I – P, Q – Z), Date modified, Type, Size, Date created, Same as sort (groups that follow the sort), or (None). Downloads is grouped by date modified until you choose otherwise there. Sort also has a Folders first switch. Each folder remembers the view you give it, as in Windows 11. More options (…) is laid out as Windows 11’s. In a folder it has Undo and Redo while there is something to undo or redo, Pin to Quick access (Unpin from Quick access in a pinned folder), Select all, Select none, Invert selection, Select items matching…, Properties (of the selected items, or of the folder) and Options. In This PC and Network it has Map network drive, Add a network location, which starts at a web address, and Disconnect network drive, which lists the connected shares, in place of Pin. View lists Extra large, Large, Medium and Small icons, List, Details, Tiles and Content (Ctrl+Shift+1 to 8, as in Windows), then Details pane (Alt+Shift+P) and Preview pane (Alt+P), which take turns in the pane at the right as in Windows, and Show, which holds Navigation pane, Compact view, Item check boxes, File name extensions and Hidden items (Ctrl+H); Split view, Folder tree and Terminal follow. As in Windows, file name extensions are hidden for known file types until you turn on View → Show → File name extensions or clear Folder Options → View → Hide extensions for known file types: Notes.txt shows as Notes, folders and unknown types keep their whole names, and renaming keeps the extension. On This PC a saved share is named like a Windows mapped drive, such as Backup (\\fileserver) (S:), with a bar showing its free space while it is connected. Settings → Appearance chooses Light, Dark or the system appearance. More options → Options opens Folder Options. Its View tab has Folder views: Apply to Folders gives every folder, Downloads included, the view of the folder you opened it from (layout, icon size, columns, sort and grouping), and Reset Folders gives every folder the default view, Details sorted by name, with Downloads grouped by date again. Each asks Yes or No first. OpenXplorer has no folder types, so both cover all folders; Apply to Folders is unavailable from This PC, Network, Recent, search results and the Recycle Bin. The View tab also turns off Remember each folder's view settings (then every folder shares one view), shows hidden files in every folder (as Ctrl+H does), and has Always show icons, never thumbnails. The View tab's Advanced settings also show or hide the status bar and the pop-up descriptions of items, choose whether the Preview pane shows a file's contents, and, under When typing into list view, send what you type in the file list to the search box. The General tab's Open File Explorer to chooses Home or This PC for new windows; Browse folders can open each folder you open from the file list in its own window; Privacy shows or hides Recent files and Recent locations in the navigation pane, and Clear File Explorer history forgets them and the addresses you typed. Single-click opening is not available yet, so only Double-click can be chosen. Its More settings… keeps your choices and opens Settings (Ctrl+, opens it too). The Search tab's Always search file names and contents makes searches look inside files from the start. Dates are shown in full with the time, as in Windows Explorer, and a folder's Size is empty; Settings → Files & folders → Relative dates (Today, Yesterday) and Show the number of items in folders turn on Dolphin's way. If you turned on the number of items in folders in 2.0.11 or earlier, turn it on again once: those versions saved it the same way as their default.

sections.title: Two folders in one tab
paragraphs: Choose View → Split view to open two panes. Click either pane to make its path, selection and commands active. Each pane keeps its own folder and history. Choosing Split view again closes the active pane and keeps the other.

Settings → General → Start up lets you choose where new windows open and turn on Reopen my tabs when OpenXplorer starts. Session restoration is off by default. New tabs normally open beside the current tab.

sections.title: Previews and the folder tree
paragraphs: Settings → Files & folders → Previews and thumbnails controls thumbnail previews, file types and the large-file limit. Previews in network folders are off by default. Missing previews use the desktop thumbnail service when available; supported local images can be generated by OpenXplorer. Files that cannot be previewed keep their icons.

The Details pane (View → Details pane, or Alt+Shift+P as in Windows) is laid out like Windows 11’s: a large preview of the selected file, its icon and name, Share, then Details with its Type, Size, File location, Date modified and Date created, and a Properties button. Dates show the day and the time, as in the file list. A photo adds its date taken, dimensions and camera (maker, model, F-stop, exposure time, ISO speed, focal length, flash), and audio or video its length, bit rate and artists, read as the Properties Details tab reads them, a moment after the selection settles, without slowing the window. Several selected items show how many there are and the total size of the files among them; with nothing selected it names the folder and counts what the list shows, a search’s results included, as in “Downloads (2 items)”, over Windows’ hint to select a single file. A selected folder lists its type, location and date modified. Right-click the pane to choose its rows. As in Windows, the pane has no close button: Alt+Shift+P, View or the Details button hides it.

View → Folder tree (F7) shows a tree of folders below the navigation places. Expand a folder to read its subfolders. Its menu controls hidden folders, limiting the tree to Home and following the active folder. The arrows beside This PC and Network collapse and expand those sections; with the keyboard, press Left or Right on the section’s name. Settings → Appearance → Layout → Hide expand arrows shows the navigation pane’s arrows only while you point at the pane or move through it with the keyboard, as in Windows. Recent locations lists folders from desktop history and offers Clear recent locations.

sections.title: Templates, shortcuts and help
paragraphs: New lists what Windows 11 lists: Folder, Shortcut, Bitmap image, Rich Text Document, Text Document and Compressed (zipped) Folder. Each new item is made at once, as “New Text Document.txt” for example, or “New Text Document (2).txt” when that name is taken, and renamed in place. Your Templates folder adds its files after them, with its subfolders as submenus; a template is copied under its own name the same way. Creating never overwrites an existing file.

Settings → About → Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+?) lists the available keys; Settings → About also has Help (F1), License & source and About this build. Windows Explorer’s keys work too: Ctrl+E and F3 move to the search box like Ctrl+F, Ctrl+D moves the selection to the Recycle Bin like Delete (a text field keeps it), Alt+P shows the details pane like Alt+Shift+P, and F11 shows the window full screen until you press it again. F1 opens the built-in manual without a network connection. Report an issue opens the project issue tracker only when selected.

sections.title: Rename an item
paragraphs: Press F2, or choose Rename, and the name becomes a text field in its row or tile, with a file’s name before its extension selected. Press Enter or click elsewhere to keep the new name, or Escape to keep the old one. As in Windows, the characters \ / : * ? " < > | can’t be typed or pasted into the name: nothing is inserted, and a balloon under the field says “A file name can’t contain any of the following characters”. A name that already has one keeps it while you edit it.

If another file in the folder already has the name you type, the Rename File question offers the next free numbered name, such as Report (2).txt: Yes renames the file to it, and No lets you edit the name again. A folder given a name that is taken is not renamed, and nothing is ever overwritten.

sections.title: Rename several items at once
paragraphs: As in Windows Explorer, select several items and press F2, or choose Rename, then type one name for the item whose name opens for editing and press Enter. Every selected item gets that name with a number in brackets, in the order the folder shows them: Holiday (1).jpg, Holiday (2).jpg, Holiday (3).png. Each file keeps its own extension, and folders and files without an extension get none. A numbered name that is already taken is skipped, so nothing is overwritten. Escape renames nothing, an item that cannot be renamed is listed in Operation result while the others are renamed, and one Ctrl+Z renames them all back.

To number items your own way, right-click the selection, choose Show more options if you use the Windows 11 menu, then Rename items…. Its dialog gives every item one name with # replaced by an ascending number, from the number you choose (Holiday ### gives Holiday 001.jpg, Holiday 002.jpg), and each file keeps its extension. One Ctrl+Z undoes that too.

sections.title: Follow file operations
paragraphs: Copy, move and delete jobs show in a small progress window of their own, as in Windows Explorer: it appears when a job takes more than a moment, is titled with the job's percentage (“44% complete”) or, with several jobs, “2 Running Actions”, and closes when the last job ends. Each job says what it does, such as “Copying 12 items from Projects to Archive” (click a folder to open it), and has its own Pause and Cancel. More details shows a speed graph, the item being handled, the time remaining and the items remaining; the window remembers the choice. Closing the window cancels its jobs; finished items stay.

Up to four independent jobs can run while you browse. A job that overlaps an active source or destination must wait for that job to finish. Rename, archive operations, restore and Undo run on their own. If an item fails, OpenXplorer asks as Windows 11 does: File Access Denied, Destination Folder Access Denied, File In Use or Item Not Found, with the item's name, type, size and date. Try Again, Skip and Cancel let you choose how to continue, and Do this for all current items skips every later failure. When the destination drive is full, the progress window says how much space is needed, with Try Again and Cancel. Inside a folder, only the file that fails is asked about, and the rest of the folder is still copied. Nothing more is said afterwards about what you answered. A folder you may not open shows Location is not available, and you stay in the folder you were in.

When a copy or move meets files that already have the same names, OpenXplorer asks as Windows 11 does. The files without a conflict are copied first; then the job in the progress window shows Replace or Skip Files in place of its progress: “The destination already has a file named "report.png"” with Replace the file in the destination, Skip this file and Compare info for both files, or, for several, “The destination has 3 files with the same names” with Replace the files in the destination, Skip these files and Let me decide for each file. A folder that meets a folder of its name is merged without asking, and only the files inside with the same names count. Compare info or Let me decide opens the File Conflict window, which blocks only the progress window: check the files to keep on each side, with their thumbnails, dates and sizes (Files from … and Files already in … check a whole side), or Skip the files with the same date and size, then Continue. Checking both versions keeps both, and the copied file gets a number, as report (2).png. A replaced file goes to the Recycle Bin first where the drive has one, so Undo (Ctrl+Z) brings it back; Closing the window (or the job's Cancel, when other jobs run beside it) stops the job and keeps what it already copied.

sections.title: Add installed service actions
paragraphs: Choose Configure service actions from a folder or item menu, enable the installed actions you trust, then Save. Matching enabled actions appear under Service actions. Edited definitions must be enabled again.

OpenXplorer reads supported KDE service-menu definitions and executable Nautilus scripts from XDG data folders. Selected paths are passed as separate arguments. Terminal launchers, interpreter commands and embedded field substitutions are unsupported.

sections.title: Open a protected folder
paragraphs: Open as administrator on a local folder’s menu asks for confirmation before opening an admin:/// location. GVfs requests desktop authentication through polkit; OpenXplorer itself keeps running as your user. The feature needs your distribution’s GVfs administrator backend.
Administrator access does not remove OpenXplorer’s protection of snapshot folders. Restoring a session reopens administrator locations with ordinary permissions.

sections.title: Choose your context menu
paragraphs: The Windows 11-style compact menu is the default, as on the Menu key, with the classic menu behind Show more options, on Shift+F10 and on Shift+right-click; Settings can make the Windows 10-style classic menu the default instead. If you chose the classic menu in 2.0.11 or earlier, choose it again once: those versions saved it the same way as their default. Open with uses registered applications; identical editor names are deduplicated. Its chooser works like Windows 11's: the current default and suggested apps first, every other app under More apps, then Just once or Always (which makes the app the default for that file type); Choose an app on your PC runs a program file, and Use a custom command… runs a command line with the file.

sections.title: Send files with Send to
paragraphs: The classic menu (Show more options, Shift+F10) has Windows Explorer’s Send to submenu. In Windows’ order it offers Bluetooth device, Compressed (zipped) folder, Desktop (create shortcut), Documents, Mail recipient, then each removable drive and each saved network location under the name This PC shows, such as Backup (\\fileserver) (S:). Entries that come from other applications are not added.

Documents, a drive or a network location get a copy, with the same name-conflict questions, progress and Undo as a paste, and the items you sent stay selected. Compressed (zipped) folder makes a ZIP beside the items, as Compress to ZIP file does. Desktop (create shortcut) puts a shortcut on the Desktop named as Windows names it, report.txt - Shortcut, then report.txt - Shortcut (2) when that name is taken; it never replaces anything, a very long name is shortened before its extension so the shortcut still fits, and Ctrl+Z moves the shortcuts to the Recycle Bin. A shortcut is a symbolic link, so a location without symbolic links, such as a share opened through GVfs or a FAT-formatted USB stick, says so instead.

Mail recipient opens a new message in your email app with the files attached, as Share does, and Bluetooth device hands the files to your desktop’s Bluetooth sender (GNOME Bluetooth, Blueman or KDE’s BlueDevil), which asks for the device. Each appears only when the computer has it: Bluetooth needs an adapter and a sender, Mail recipient the desktop’s email portal. An entry that cannot run is greyed out and its tooltip says why: Bluetooth and Mail recipient take files only, Desktop (create shortcut) is unavailable in a previous version, and the copies and the shortcut wait while your other file operations leave no room for them. In Recent files, Send to sends the file each row stands for. A saved network location that is not connected is offered too: choosing it connects it first, asking you to sign in if the server needs it, then copies.

sections.title: Share files by email
paragraphs: Share in the command bar, between Rename and Delete as in Windows 11, opens a new message in your email app with the selected files attached. It goes through your desktop’s email portal (KDE Plasma’s, or GTK’s on GNOME), and nothing is sent until you send the message there. The Details pane has the same Share button. Share takes files, up to 16 at a time; folders, items in the Recycle Bin and items inside a ZIP cannot be shared. Where the desktop has no email portal, and in Open and Save dialogs, the button is hidden. If no email app is set up, the message at the bottom of the window says the email app could not be opened. A file whose name or folder has &, #, ?, % or a control character cannot be shared, as GNOME’s email portal could misread it, for example as an extra recipient; the message names the file, and renaming or moving it lets you share it.
To copy an item’s path instead, right-click it and choose Copy as path, or press Ctrl+Shift+C.

sections.title: Properties
paragraphs: Alt+Enter, or Properties in a right-click menu, opens Properties as Windows 11 lays it out, in a window of its own: it blocks neither the main window nor another Properties window, and asking again for the same item brings its window back. A file has General, Security, Details and Previous Versions; a folder on this computer adds Sharing and Customize, and Downloads, Documents and the other standard folders add Location.

General shows the name, Type of file and Opens with (Change… picks another app), Location, Size and Size on disk with every byte, such as 314 KB (322,003 bytes), the dates in the long style, such as Tuesday, October 20, 2026, 14:24:52, and the Read-only and Hidden attributes. A folder counts its Size, Size on disk and Contains by itself and shows Created only. Hidden adds a dot to the start of the name, which is how Linux hides an item. With several items selected, the title names the first two, such as a.txt, b.txt, ... Properties, and Read-only and Hidden show a half tick where the items differ; ticking or clearing one changes every item on OK or Apply.

Changes wait for OK or Apply: Apply stays grey until something changes, OK applies and closes, and Cancel or Escape closes without changing anything. A refused change, such as a name that is taken, shows in a message and Properties stays open.

Security shows the item’s real Linux permissions in Windows’ words: the owner, the group and everyone else, and what the one selected may do, from Full control to Read. Edit… and Advanced change them when you own the item; Linux has no deny entries, so the Deny column stays empty. Customize holds Change Icon… for a folder, which lists your icon theme’s folder icons, with Browse… for a picture of your own.

Details lists what a file says about itself under Windows’ headings, Property on the left and Value on the right: for a photo its title, rating stars, authors, date taken, dimensions, resolution and the camera’s EXIF (maker, model, F-stop, exposure time, ISO speed, focal length, flash), for a video its length, frame size, data rate and frame rate, for a song its artists, album, year, track number, genre, length, bit rate, channels and sample rate, and for every file its name, type, folder, dates, size, attributes and owner. Rows OpenXplorer cannot read on Linux are left out rather than shown empty, and the values cannot be changed here. The arrow keys move through the list, Ctrl+C copies the value of the row you are on, and Enter, F2 or a click in a value lets you select part of it. The file is read in the background and given up after 10 seconds, so a slow share or a large or damaged file never holds Properties up. Windows’ Remove Properties and Personal Information is not offered yet, as it cannot be done safely for every kind of file the tab shows.

sections.title: Previous versions
paragraphs: Properties → Previous Versions lists existing, exposed snapshot collections under Name and Date modified, grouped by date as Windows 11 groups them. Select a version: Open shows it in a new tab, and Restore writes a copy to a separate destination, never over the live original. Snapshot source… sets where versions are looked for, and F5 looks again.
This provider recognizes exposed filesystem directories. It does not implement the Windows SMB shadow-copy enumeration protocol, create snapshots, or make backup history exist on a server.

Each version shows the item’s name and, under Date modified, the date and time read from recognized snapshot names, including auto-2026-09-04_16-30, 2026-09-05_180000, and @GMT names; the row’s tooltip names the snapshot, where it came from and where its date comes from. Unrecognized names show “Date unavailable”; folder modification times are not passed off as snapshot creation times.
@GMT timestamps are marked UTC. Other names are shown as written, without guessing a server timezone. This is display metadata, not a server-side ZFS creation-property query.

Snapshot tabs carry a “Previous version” badge and an amber top edge. A banner identifies the historical view and its read-only treatment in OpenXplorer, including when browsing deeper inside it. Network snapshot tabs keep their green network marker. Properties is a window of its own, so it stays open beside the snapshot tab.
sections.imageAlt: Snapshot list with a separate right-hand date and time column

sections.title: Measure folder sizes on demand
paragraphs: Calculate folder size totals accessible logical file sizes on a worker with progress and cancellation, and shows them in the Size column. Properties counts a folder by itself as soon as it opens, as Windows Explorer does: Size, Size on disk and Contains climb while the folder is measured, and closing Properties stops the count. A drive's Properties shows what Windows 11's does instead: its label, type and file system, its used and free space and capacity in bytes and GB, and a ring of the two, without counting anything on it; where it is mounted and from what are on its Hardware tab. Limits, excluded entries and read errors are shown as incomplete coverage. Results are session-only and can become stale.

Size counts logical file bytes; Size on disk counts the blocks the files take, which on a compressing filesystem such as ZFS is the compressed space. Neither is a ZFS dataset used/referenced value or a snapshot-exclusive block count.

sections.title: Browse a ZIP, without extracting everything
paragraphs: ZIP browsing is read-only. Listing reads archive metadata; opening a selected member decompresses that member into a private temporary copy. Archive modifications, encrypted archives and unsupported formats require an external application.

sections.title: Extract ZIP files
paragraphs: Select a ZIP and click Extract all in the command bar, or right-click it and choose Extract all… in either context-menu style. As in Windows Explorer, one field says where the files go, filled in with the ZIP's folder and name (for example Downloads/tidewater); Browse… picks another folder. A folder that does not exist yet is created. Delete the last part to extract straight into an existing folder such as Downloads: if a file with the same name is already there, you are asked whether to replace or skip it. A ZIP holding one folder of the same name is not nested (no tidewater/tidewater). The ZIP stays unchanged, and Cancel is available in the progress window. The ⓘ button at the bottom left shows how many files the ZIP holds, a few notes, and Open in archive manager, which opens your archive manager (such as Ark) even when OpenXplorer opens ZIPs by default. A password-protected ZIP cannot be extracted here: the dialog says so and offers the archive manager.

ZIPs open like folders, as in Windows Explorer (Settings → ZIP & archives → Double-clicking a ZIP → Like a folder, the default). Opening a ZIP shows it in the tab: the address bar shows the path through it, folders inside open in the tab, Back and Up work, and Extract all appears in the bar. The ZIP stays read-only; Copy (then Paste anywhere) and dragging items out hand over real copies, which OpenXplorer unpacks into ~/.cache/winspace/zip-copies and removes after a day. Choose In a pop-up window to open ZIPs in the Compressed folder window instead.

Local and already connected SMB locations are supported by the implementation; live SMB extraction still needs target-machine validation. Sign into the relevant shares first. Password-protected ZIPs, unsupported methods, and files exceeding the built-in safety limits need an external archive manager. Double-click continues to browse without extracting the entire ZIP.

sections.title: Make text easier to read
paragraphs: Ctrl + (or Ctrl =) increases text, Ctrl − decreases it, and Ctrl 0 resets to 100%. Settings → Appearance → Text size offers 80% through 200%. The preference is saved across restarts and applied to open windows.
Only the application text and needed row spacing change; desktop scaling and file data remain unchanged. Sidebar and column widths remain resizable.

sections.title: Open in Terminal
paragraphs: Right-click a folder, sidebar pin or the file-list background and choose Open in Terminal. Right-click a regular file to open its containing folder. Both context-menu styles include the command.

A connected SMB location needs a usable local CIFS or GVfs-FUSE mount. The shell runs on your Linux computer, not on the NAS. No SSH session or remote command is created. Server listings, ZIP contents and protected snapshot views cannot be used as a terminal directory.

The system terminal alternative is used when supported; otherwise an installed GNOME Terminal, Console, Xfce Terminal, Konsole or XTerm is selected. Paths are passed as literal arguments and working directories, not shell command strings. View → Terminal opens the configured external terminal; the website tour shows pictures and starts no program.

sections.title: Middle-click and move tabs
paragraphs: Middle-click a folder, connected share, breadcrumb or sidebar location to open a background tab. Shift+middle-click also switches to it. Middle-click an existing tab to close it. Background directories load when selected, so opening a network tab does not immediately interrupt you with a login dialog.

Press a tab to show it, then drag it along its strip: the other tabs slide aside as it moves, and it stays where you release it. Drag it out of the strip and the tab itself follows the pointer while the tab beside it comes to the front: over another OpenXplorer window's tab strip it joins that strip, whose tabs make room for it, and a release there merges it at that spot, while a release outside every tab strip opens it in a new window. With no other OpenXplorer window open, the only tab of a window takes the window along. The Move tab to new window menu remains available. Escape cancels and keeps the tab, with one exception: on Wayland, Escape pressed while the pointer is outside every OpenXplorer window goes to the desktop, not to OpenXplorer, and the desktop reports it as a drag that ended there, so the tab opens in a new window. The original tab is kept until the destination acknowledges it.

sections.title: Drag files between applications
paragraphs: Select one or more files or folders and drag them into an application that accepts native file drops. The desktop app supplies file URIs and readable paths through GTK, including already-mounted network paths when available. Ctrl-click or Shift-click to select multiple items. Press Escape to cancel.

Drop files into an OpenXplorer folder, the empty area of the current folder, or another OpenXplorer window to propose a copy. As in Windows Explorer, a plain drag of OpenXplorer's own items moves them to a folder on the same drive and copies them to another drive; hold Ctrl to copy or Shift to move. A plain drag of items from another app always copies them; hold Shift to move them instead. Files with the same names are asked about in the progress window, as for Paste. Incoming data is staged before file replacement; same-name folders merge and keep destination-only entries. File/folder type conflicts are left unchanged. While you drag, a label under the dragged items says what releasing them would do, as in Windows 11: → Move to Documents, + Copy to Documents (hold Ctrl) or Create link in Documents (hold Ctrl+Shift). No label means a release there does nothing. Drop onto a folder or drive in the navigation pane to copy or move into it; drop between Quick access entries (where an accent line and Pin to Quick access show) to pin or reorder folders. Holding a drag over a folder in the file list never opens it, as in Windows 11; drop on it to copy or move into it. Holding a drag over the navigation pane never changes the folder shown either; held over a collapsed This PC or Network, it expands it. File drops never request deletion of the source.

Drag with the right mouse button to choose what happens, as in Windows Explorer. Pressing the right button selects the item; releasing it without moving opens its menu. When you release a right-button drag over a folder, a menu opens there: Copy here, Move here, Create shortcuts here and Cancel. The bold entry is what an ordinary drag would do, Move here on the same drive and Copy here on another. Only what is possible is listed: items you may not delete cannot be moved, and Create shortcuts here needs items and a folder on this computer whose drive can hold symbolic links (not FAT or exFAT). A shortcut is a symbolic link named like a Windows shortcut, such as report.txt - Shortcut, then report.txt - Shortcut (2). Dropped back in their own folder, the menu offers Copy here, which makes copies such as report - Copy.txt, and Create shortcuts here. Escape or Cancel does nothing. Once the menu is open, Up, Down and Enter choose an entry.

ZIP members must be extracted first. Some editors only accept local files: network items need an existing GVfs/FUSE or CIFS path for those applications. Dragging does not mount a share or download a temporary copy. Automatic extraction remains unavailable. Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes back a drop into an OpenXplorer folder, a copy or a move, as it takes back Paste.
The website tour shows pictures and cannot drag files. Compatibility with a particular editor or a Wayland desktop must be checked on that system.

title: Development
description: One repository. A native app and an independent website.

sections.title: Repository layout
paragraphs: native/ contains the Rust GTK 4 application, its parity inventories, packaging and check driver. The Python GTK/WebKit app of 1.x has been removed from the tree: its last release is tag v1.1.4, and its final sources, which native/parity/ cites as the behavioural specification, are desktop/ at tag v2.0.0. apps/web/ contains the Next.js App Router website. docs/ mirrors the website documentation as Markdown. designs/ holds generated standalone HTML pitches.

sections.title: Run the website with pnpm
paragraphs: Use Node.js 22.13+ and the package manager version declared at the root. The supplied pnpm-lock.yaml records resolved dependencies. Use frozen installs and review any dependency changes together with their lockfile changes. Dependencies are not vendored.
sections.code:
corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@10.34.5 --activate
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate
pnpm dev
sections.callout: Dependency installation, dependency-aware pnpm check and the real Next.js production export have passed. The production-export browser suite also passes, including React hydration, tour readiness and mobile iframe removal. Standalone HTML rendering is a separate design-review workflow; consult the current test report for each check actually executed.

sections.title: Build and validate
paragraphs: The website remains a Next.js static export. pnpm build writes apps/web/out, and pnpm check performs dependency-aware TypeScript checking. Cloudflare Workers Static Assets serves that export without a framework migration or application backend. The offline design renderer does not exercise the Next.js runtime.

The native experience roadmap and public source checklist are in docs/NATIVE-EXPERIENCE-ROADMAP.md and docs/PUBLIC-RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md. They distinguish remaining desktop work, source-publication preparation and stable-release validation.
sections.code:
pnpm check
pnpm build
pnpm preview

# Native checks and the release .deb (Ubuntu 24.04 build host)
python3 native/tools/check.py
python3 native/parity/check.py
python3 native/tools/build_deb.py --app-id io.winspace.Development
python3 native/tools/verify_deb.py dist/native/openxplorer_2.0.14_all.deb

sections.title: Make a focused contribution
paragraphs: Read CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md. Use disposable files for operation tests. Separate UI fixtures from native integration results, include reproducible steps, and do not publish NAS passwords or private filename inventories. Contributions are under the project license, with existing notices preserved.

sections.title: Compatibility identifiers
paragraphs: The visible name and public command are OpenXplorer/openxplorer. The previous io.winspace.Development desktop ID, winspace configuration paths and credential schemas remain deliberately stable. Do not bulk-rename them without a migration design.

sections.title: Regenerate the screenshots and the tour
paragraphs: The website screenshots and the click-through tour are pictures of the native app, taken by its snapshot hook (OPENXPLORER_SNAPSHOT) in an isolated session: bubblewrap hides the home folders, mounts and session bus and gives the app no network, Xvfb and a private D-Bus session keep it off the desktop, and a fictional demo tree is mounted as /home/demo. The tour's clickable areas are the rectangles of real controls, which the app reports. Do not replace the pictures with a separately drawn explorer mockup. Review every picture before committing it.
sections.code:
python3 tools/capture-screenshots.py
python3 tools/capture-native-tour.py
python3 tools/audit-public-data.py
pnpm designs
sections.callout: Capturing needs cargo, bubblewrap (bwrap), xvfb-run and dbus-run-session; the tools build the release program with the stable application ID. The pictures show fictional files and no live SMB server; they do not replace the native tests.

sections.title: Documentation as Markdown
paragraphs: Copy page as Markdown copies the full guide, including headings, paragraphs, code blocks, callouts and screenshot references—not a link or rendered HTML. The content source is apps/web/lib/docs.json; tools/sync-docs.py regenerates repository documentation and the website copies.
Documentation search opens from its named button. The site does not intercept Command-K or Control-K. Keyboard navigation within the search dialog and Escape-to-close remain available.

title: Website deployment
description: Publish a static site linked to its public source repository.

sections.title: Configure before publication
paragraphs: Edit apps/web/lib/site.ts for public identity. The canonical project URL is https://openxplorer.app.

The public source repository is https://github.com/AKolenda/openxplorer. Package calls to action link to https://github.com/AKolenda/openxplorer/releases. Source links lead to the repository. The website has no direct download links. Keep the repository public whenever the website links to it.

sections.title: Prepare a local release
paragraphs: The release tool creates and verifies a local Debian package, corresponding-source archive and checksums under dist/. It also removes any legacy website download directories. The website itself carries no release binaries; its source links lead to the public GitHub repository and its package links lead to GitHub Releases.
sections.code:
pnpm check
pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate
pnpm designs
pnpm release
python3 tools/audit-public-data.py
pnpm build

sections.title: Cloudflare Workers Static Assets
paragraphs: The root wrangler.jsonc serves apps/web/out with Cloudflare Workers Static Assets. The site remains Next.js with output: export. The configured custom domain is openxplorer.app; workers.dev and preview URLs are disabled. Directory-style HTML routing and the exported 404 page are configured.

Use the project-local Wrangler and the dedicated openxplorer OAuth profile. Named profiles are experimental in the pinned CLI and keep this project separate from default-profile authentication. CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN takes precedence over profiles; verify the active identity before publishing. Do not place credentials in source files.

After OAuth completes, activate the profile and verify its account. The local development, dry-run and deployment scripts explicitly pass --profile openxplorer. A dry run checks packaging and does not deploy. Full setup and account/domain checks are documented in docs/CLOUDFLARE-SETUP.md.
sections.code:
pnpm cf:login
pnpm cf:activate
pnpm cf:profiles
pnpm cf:whoami

# After building and auditing the release above:
pnpm cf:dry-run
pnpm cf:dev
# After reviewing the export and confirming the intended account/domain:
pnpm cf:deploy

sections.title: Automatic releases
paragraphs: Changes merged into main run on GitHub-hosted Actions runners. The workflow checks the website and desktop, verifies native file transport, packages matching installer and source archives, and publishes a new version to GitHub Releases; existing release assets are not overwritten. A separate job checks and deploys the website to Cloudflare, so a failed or skipped package release does not hold the site back. The website's download button opens GitHub's latest release and names no version.

Only `main` publishes a release or deploys the website. Cloudflare uses a dedicated secret in the `production` environment, which only `main` may deploy from; local OAuth credentials are not copied to CI. Repository configuration and recovery are documented in docs/RELEASE-WORKFLOW.md.

sections.title: Check before announcing
paragraphs: Run browser checks against the actual HTTP-served Next.js export. Test hydration, routes, keyboard navigation, mobile menus, search and every public-repository link. Confirm that no release binaries are emitted into the website export. Also verify Cloudflare routing/security headers and 404 behavior. The site has no application sign-in, analytics scripts, external fonts or tracking pixels.

The tour of the native app is embedded in an iframe with only allow-scripts; it has an opaque sandbox origin and shows only static pictures. It accepts only fixed demo commands from its parent window, and the page checks message sources before showing status. Never replace this with a native credential or filesystem bridge.

sections.title: Release launch checks
paragraphs: Dependency installation, pnpm check, the real pnpm build and production-export browser checks have passed. A dedicated Wrangler OAuth profile can deploy this site independently of the default login. Verify the current domain and deployment status before announcing a release. See TEST-REPORT.md for executed checks and docs/PUBLIC-RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md for source-publication preparation. Stable 1.0.0 is published on GitHub Releases; re-run these checks before each new release.

sections.title: Corresponding source on GitHub
paragraphs: The public GitHub repository provides the preferred editable files, build scripts, documentation and dependency declarations for this release. The website links to that repository instead of hosting its own source archive or installer. Dependencies installed unchanged from package registries or system repositories remain under their respective licenses.

When hosting a modified version that supports remote interaction, keep an appropriate offer of its corresponding source available to those users. Consult the actual license text, especially sections 6 and 13, for the conditions rather than relying on this brief description.

sections.title: Preserved notices
paragraphs: The original Winspace MIT notice is retained in licenses/Winspace-MIT.txt and packaged with the application. AppStream metadata remains CC0-1.0. Next.js, React and other dependencies are not relicensed by this project. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

sections.title: An independent project
paragraphs: Windows, Windows File Explorer, Zorin OS, Ubuntu, Debian and Vercel are names of their respective owners. OpenXplorer is not affiliated with or endorsed by those projects. The design directions are inspired by familiar interaction and visual styles; no Microsoft or Zorin artwork or proprietary fonts is bundled.

sections.title: Project identity before publication
paragraphs: The canonical project domain is openxplorer.app and the public source repository is https://github.com/AKolenda/openxplorer. The website does not host release downloads. Use genuine maintainer/contact details when they are added and do not fabricate usage statistics or support claims.
